To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

saline bolus tests are sensitive to peripheral, as well as proximal, airway alterations and that the former can be detected by measuring the bolus half-width at low VLD, whereas the latter are best identified by measuring the dispersion at high VLD.

saline aerosol boluses, when inhaled in a controlled manner, are dispersed in a manner that depends on the site of airway alteration and that this dispersion can be quantified to detect proximal as well as peripheral alterations.

1) the saline bolus test is a reliable method for the assessment of peripheral airway alteration and 2) to assess proximal airway alterations, the test should include measurements at low VLD and should quantify bolus dispersion by a standard deviation with low cutoff.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method to detect proximal airway alterations.
the development of a noninvasive test for the detection of proximal airway alterations.
the use of saline aerosol boluses to assess the distribution of ventilation within the lungs and with its application to the study of the pathophysiology of asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
saline bolus tests can detect both proximal and peripheral airway alterations but that the latter can be detected only if bolus dispersion at high VLD is assessed.

the saline bolus dispersion technique is able to identify peripheral airway alteration but not proximal airway obstruction, and that the latter can be detected with the saline bolus technique only if the technique is applied with a low cutoff and at low and high volumetric lung depths.
saline bolus tests can detect proximal airway alterations, but only if they are performed at low and high lung depths and if bolus concentrations are measured down to low cutoffs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for a bolus test to detect proximal airway alterations, it is necessary to measure bolus dispersion at low and high volumetric lung depths and to quantify this dispersion by a standard deviation with low cutoffs.
, for proximal airway alterations, the saline bolus dispersion index is a function of the VLD and the bolus dispersion quantification method.
the saline bolus test can identify peripheral airway alterations, whereas proximal airway alterations are identified only if the bolus dispersion index is quantified at both low and high V LD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
saline bolus tests are sensitive to both proximal and distal airway alterations and, thus, can be used to detect airway disease of various etiologies.
, when properly performed, saline aerosol boluses can be a powerful tool for detecting and characterizing airway disease.

saline bolus tests can be used to detect airway alteration in the central airways as well as in the periphery, but that the choice of the bolus dispersion index and of the VLD at which measurements are performed is of crucial importance.
